newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels fire at army vehicle, wound four.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels fire at army vehicle, wound four.

text.p: Separatist guerrillas lobbed grenades and fired at an army vehicle in the rebels' former Jaffna stronghold, wounding four soldiers, the Defence Ministry said on Sunday.
The attack occurred at Neerveli in the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo on Saturday, the statement said.
It did not say whether anybody was killed in the attack, but said the wounded were moved to a military hopital in nearby Palaly.
Jaffna was controlled by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels for nearly a decade but was captured by government forces last year after a lenghty offensive.
The rebels, who have now set up base in the Wanni region south of the peninsula, continue to attack military targets in the peninsula.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.

Military officials in the north said on Sunday that the rebels had launched an attack on the military's forward defences at Omanthai, near Vavuniya, late on Saturday. Vavuniya lies some 220 km (137 miles) north of Colombo.
They said the guerrillas attacked defences manned by police. One policeman was wounded in the attack, which was repulsed, they added.
A Defence Ministry spokesman in Colombo said there were no details available immediately.
A rebel statement issued from their London office said on Sunday that government troops had fired at civilians in Jaffna during a search operation last Tuesday, killing four men.
"Their bodies were left strewn on the roadside in order to terrorise Tamil residents," the statement added.
The rebels have mounted sporadic attacks on the troops in recent weeks after the military launched one of its biggest operations against the LTTE last month.

Some 20,000 troops launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru, or "Sure of Victory", through the brush jungles of the Wanni in an attempt to open a key highway linking Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The troops, moving on two flanks, captured key rebel towns in the Wanni before the rebels struck at the army's rear earlier this month, killing nearly 150 soldiers after fierce fighting.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as interanatonal media has not been allowed in the war zone.
